page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Set up cos3θ = −cos2θ
steps.margin_note: First mark. 36° is one fifth of 180°, so 2θ and 3θ are supplementary and cos3θ = −cos2θ. Expand both sides.
steps.memory_tip: 36° is one fifth of 180°, so 3θ = 180° − 2θ and cos3θ = −cos2θ.

recall.must_convey: That 5θ = 180° gives 3θ = 180° − 2θ, so cos3θ = −cos2θ, and both sides are expanded.

steps.why: 36° is one fifth of 180°. That is the only special fact about it, and it is what turns the question into an equation in cosθ.

steps.label: Solve for cosθ
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The cubic factors as (c + 1)(4c² − 2c − 1). Reject c = −1 because 36° is not 180°, then take the positive root. A shorter route if sin18° = (√5 − 1)/4 is already known: cos36° = 1 − 2sin²18° gives the same value.
steps.memory_tip: Factor out (c + 1) and reject it, since 36° is not 180°. Then take the positive root.

recall.must_convey: That the cubic factors, c = −1 is rejected, and the positive root of 4c² − 2c − 1 = 0 is (√5 + 1)/4.

steps.why: c = −1 does solve the cubic, because cos180° = −1 also satisfies 3θ = 180° − 2θ. It has to be rejected by name, since θ here is 36° and not 180°.
